sections.title: Weight and Balance
notes: PROPOSED--"The purpose of Service Letter #304 is to describe the proper procedure for establishing a special purpose operating weight that is higher than the FAA certificated gross weight of the AT-402 series. Service Letter #80AA was previously issued to address this subject, but the subject is worth additional clarification. The 402-series Air Tractor aircraft are certificated in the FAA's RESTRICTED category, which allows the aircraft to be used for agricultural dispersal purposes. When these aircraft are operating in the RESTRICTED category, the operator may use the guidance provided in CAM 8 and FAA Advisory Circular No. 20-33B to operate at weights higher than the certificated gross weight that is listed in the Flight Manual. The methods described in CAM 8 should be used to approve your aircraft for operation at these higher weights. Service Letter #304 provides guidance and clarification that will assist you in properly following the CAM 8 methods."--PROPOSED ADDITIONS TO INCORPORATE SL#80AA AND SL#304.

sections.title: Horizontal Stabilizers
notes: PROPOSED--"Reports have been received of large birds striking the outboard end of the horizontal tail on various aircraft. In a few cases, the bird impacted near the gap between the elevator horn and the horizontal stabilizer. The damaged surface was pushed into the gap and caused the elevator horn to become obstructed. To help prevent the likelihood of jamming, Air Tractor is installing perforated ribs in the elevators and stabilizers of new aircraft.

Air Tractor recommends that all operators, especially those who operate in areas where impact with large birds are likely to have their aircraft modified to perforate the ribs of this area. The perforated ribs will allow the unsupported tip of the nose rib to break free if it becomes damaged and reduce the risk of binding. This change will also remove two non-structural closeout plates on those aircraft that have them installed. Refer to Service Letter #319 for additional information."--PROPOSED to reference SL #319. PROPOSED -- "For AT-402A-1361 & prior and AT-402B-1361 & prior--we have become aware that the fuel drain valve on the bottom of the firewall mounted fuel filter has the potential to become damaged in flight. This damage most likely would come from a bird strike on the fuel drain valve. If an object such as a bird were to hit the drain valve in flight with enough force it could be broken or cracked and leak fuel. If a leak occurred, it is also possible that air would be sucked into the fuel system. Air sucked into the fuel system could cause a loss of engine power and the engine may flame out. To prevent an occurrence as described here, a deflector/guard for the drain valve has been designed that is fully described in Service Letter #343." -- PROPOSED FOR INSERTION TO INCORPORATE SL#343.
